risk_if_not_implemented: Without Export Activities Documentation, the organization may fail to meet statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations, or be unable to demonstrate conformity when required. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Loss of Investigative / Evidentiary Capability (R-IR-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) (TPM-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Export Activities Documentation (CPL-24.3) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Dual Use Technology
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to govern technologies and/or data that have potential:
(1) "Dual-use” capabilities for civil and military;
(2) Use by terrorists; and/or 
(3) Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) applications.
compensating_control_2.justification: Dual Use Technology (CPL-24) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Export Activities Documentation (CPL-24.3) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
